subject: Model slate selection and request-pattern forecast for PilotAI onboarding
messages:
From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@pilotai.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: onboard@pilotai.com
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PilotAI onboarding — request-pattern snapshot and context needs

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to move toward a production integration with Redwood. Ahead of the kickoff workshop next week, I wanted to share a short snapshot of how our traffic looks so you can recommend model candidates and an initial sizing estimate. I've attached a small sample of logs (pilotai_traffic_sample_20280629.jsonl).

Quick context:
- Product: PilotAI assistant inside our web app (mainly customer support augmentation).
- Primary endpoint: assistant.generate (single-turn and short multi-turn summaries).
- Typical input sources: user query (200–800 chars) + recent chat history (0–3 turns) + metadata.

Traffic profile (last 30 days):
- Average requests per hour: 480 (peaks to ~3.2k during US business hours).
- Token mix (approx): 60% requests < 512 tokens total, 30% between 512–2048, 10% > 2048 (rare, mostly agent escalations).
- Context window requirement: we need support up to ~8k tokens for the escalation path but will default to 2k for the majority of calls.

As a starting ask: can you propose a 3–4 model shortlist (latency vs cost tradeoffs) and a simple hourly token forecast for initial Dedicated capacity planning? Also, please flag any questions about caching, KV reuse, or routing that we should cover in the workshop.

Thanks — attaching the sample now.

Tom
Tom Keller
Head of Product, PilotAI
Onboard: +1 415-555-0133

Attachments: pilotai_traffic_sample_20280629.jsonl (sample, 5k rows)
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@pilotai.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PilotAI onboarding — request-pattern snapshot and context needs

Tom — thanks for the sample and the clear summary. Looping in Grace (CS lead) and Vivek (solutions eng) so we can align the sizing and model recommendations before the workshop.

High-level answers up front:
- We'll draft a 3-model shortlist covering a low-latency option, a cost-optimized option, and a high-context option for your escalation path.
- Prefix/KV caching looks valuable: for sessions where a user repeatedly queries the same document, caching can cut token generation by ~20–40% depending on reuse.
- For initial Dedicated sizing, we'll produce an hourly token forecast using your provided mix and an expected ramp (MVP week: 50% of current traffic; week 4: 100% with 20% headroom).

Immediate ask for the workshop prep:
1) Can you confirm the fraction of calls that must preserve full 8k context vs those that can truncate to 2k? (Your sample suggests ~2–3% but we want an exact SLA for routing.)
2) Any latency SLO you need for the main endpoint (p50/p95)?
3) Do you expect sudden scheduled spikes (e.g., new feature releases) or mostly organic peaks?

I'll attach a draft mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) and a one-page cost/latency snapshot for three candidate model classes ahead of tomorrow's sync. Proposed shortlist (preliminary):
- rw-highthroughput-7b-qat: low latency, good cost efficiency for <2k context.
- open-llama-30b-sparse: higher context and quality for heavy summarization but higher cost.
- rw-13b-cuopt: mid-point — reasonable latency and better long-context behavior with quantized kernels.

We'll iterate once Grace reviews the traffic sample.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 650-555-0172

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-07-01T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PilotAI onboarding — request-pattern snapshot and context needs

Thanks — I dug into the attached sample and ran a quick baseline pass. Below is a conservative operational sizing and model recommendation for the kickoff deck. I left margin buffers for initial uncertainty.

Observed sample (sanity summary):
- Sample covers 72 hours, 12k requests.
- Average token per request (input+output): 620 tokens.
- High-decile requests (top 10%) average ~2,900 tokens.
- ~2.4% of requests exceed 4k tokens; ~0.6% exceed 6k.

Operational forecast (first 30 days, production ramp to 100% by day 28):
- Baseline average RPH (requests/hour): 480 -> expected production steady-state 480
- Peak RPH (US business hours): 3,200 -> plan for sustained bursts to 4,000 RPH with autoscale headroom.
- Token throughput steady-state: avg 480 * 620 = ~298k tokens/hour. Peak (4k RPH) * 620 = 2.48M tokens/hour. Add 20% headroom -> plan for 3.0M tokens/hour peak capacity.

Model sizing recommendation:
- Latency-sensitive path (customer-facing quick suggestions): rw-highthroughput-7b-qat on Dedicated with continuous batching and a target p95 < 350ms for requests <2k tokens.
- Cost/quality balance (primary generation for most flows): rw-13b-cuopt — expect ~30–50% higher token cost vs 7b but improved coherence for multi-turn.
- Long-context / escalation path: open-llama-30b-sparse or an optimized 13b with extended context kernels; route requests >4k tokens here with a fallback that truncates to last 2k for non-critical queries.

Caching and routing notes:
- Enable prefix caching for session-level reuse; expect 10–25% token savings in first 30 days.
- Two-tier routing: default route -> 7b (fast); if >2k tokens or quality score triggers -> 13b or 30b. Automatic fallback: if 30b capacity constrained, route to 13b with notice and degraded-quality flag.

Preliminary cost signal (very rough):
- 7b-qat Dedicated: baseline $X/token (internal calc) — recommended capacity to cover 2.0–2.5M tokens/hour with burst lanes.
- 13b-cuopt: ~1.4x cost of 7b.
- 30b-sparse: ~3x cost of 7b (use sparingly for escalations).

Deliverables for the workshop:
- Final 3-model shortlist + performance envelope.
- Hourly token forecast spreadsheet (I attached a reduced CSV in the Drive link).
- Routing and caching decision tree for implementation.

I'll present the sizing slide and the routing diagram. Vivek, can you validate kernel/quantization constraints for the 13b option before the workshop?

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: traffic_analysis_notes.txt (summary), traffic_sample_highlights.csv

Lauren / Grace / Vivek — this all looks great, thanks for the fast turnaround.

Quick replies:
- Confirming our SLA for escalation path: requests that mark an internal "escalation=true" flag must preserve full context up to 8k tokens ~95% of the time; those are approx 0.6–1% of total traffic.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms for the primary quick-suggestion endpoint. For escalation flows we can accept higher p95 (up to 2s).
- We do run predictable spikes tied to product release waves (roughly monthly) and will provide a 72-hour heads-up if we expect any 2x+ traffic events.

Please include a short security questionnaire in the kickoff pack — I've attached our standard form (security_questionnaire.pdf). Also, can you add a rough monthly expense band for the three model lanes (low/med/high) so our finance team has a ballpark before the kickoff?

We accept the proposed workshop time: Thursday 10am PT. See you then.

Tom
Tom Keller
Head of Product, PilotAI
